thread:
allen: Escalation from billing — customer reports SSE streaming that cuts off after ~65s, client reconnects, then gets 401 and duplicate billing entries. Fronting is Cloudflare -> ALB -> pods. Seen across multiple regions. Can we triage?

maya: Can you paste the exact root request and response headers from the failed session? any trace-id? which model/route?

allen: route: /v1/stream/chat, model: rwd-3b, credit account id 12345-prod. Trace: trace=tr-9a8f7c6d. Sample curl they used:

allen: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/chat -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```

allen: Logs from ingress (ALB) show connection idle close at 60.000s then client reconnect immediately. App logs show partial SSE events then stream closed, then reconnection with same token yields 401: "invalid_token" (but token was valid earlier).

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-874 (link internal) — assigned to eng-runtime.

devon: This smells like idle timeout + proxy buffering + auth refresh race. ALB default idle timeout 60s; Cloudflare front has its own origin timeout (~100s) and may coalesce. If client sits idle waiting for events, ALB can half-close and the app sees EOF. When client reconnects, token refresh path sometimes fails (we've seen expired short-lived tokens on reconnect).

maya: Repro plan: 1) Run a repro client that stays idle and waits for SSE prefix, 2) Force no heartbeats, 3) Observe when ALB sends RST/FIN. I can run an internal repro from eu-west-1.

devon: Quick mitigation for affected customers: enable server-side heartbeat (periodic comment SSE: `:hb\n\n`) every 25s; or increase ALB idle timeout to 120s for the target group while we investigate. Also ensure `Connection: keep-alive` and `proxy_buffering off` on any nginx fronting proxies.

leo: FYI billing: duplicate billing entries are likely because every reconnect creates a new billing session id before we validate the token fully. I've paused auto-invoicing for account 12345-prod and flagged refunds to billing ops. Need exact session ids for reconciliation.

maya: Can you attach a server-side log snippet around trace tr-9a8f7c6d? looking for SSE write() syscalls and any EPIPE or ECONNRESET. Also need ALB logs (target:target_status, elb_status) and Cloudflare ray id.

allen: Pasting sanitized logs:

allen: ```
[2026-03-17T15:03:21Z] trace=tr-9a8f7c6d stream_write: sent event id=1
[2026-03-17T15:04:10Z] trace=tr-9a8f7c6d stream_write: sent event id=2
[2026-03-17T15:04:20Z] trace=tr-9a8f7c6d transport: write failed: errno=32 EPIPE
[2026-03-17T15:04:20Z] trace=tr-9a8f7c6d connection: half-closed by proxy
[2026-03-17T15:04:21Z] trace=tr-9a8f7c6d auth: refresh_token flow started for session s-876
[2026-03-17T15:04:22Z] trace=tr-9a8f7c6d auth: refresh failed: upstream 401 invalid_credentials
```

maya: Ok that matches ALB closing around ~60s from first write to EOF. The auth refresh flow running during reconnect returned a 401 from auth-service. That explains the invalid token on reconnect, but why the auth service returning 401 right after a successful session? maybe race with short-lived tokens issued by gateway.

devon: Two hypotheses: 1) client used a one-time token that expires on reuse; reconnect tries to reuse and auth denies. 2) token refresh flow depends on sticky session/mtls info lost when ALB resets connection and Cloudflare retries to a different origin.

leo: Billing note: if reconnects are caused by our infra and result in new session starts, we should credit those sessions. I'll need a list of session ids: — s-873, s-876, s-879 from this window.

allen: Repro steps I suggested to customer (highly reproducible):
  1) Open long-poll SSE client using curl above.
  2) Do not send any client-side pings. Wait ~70s.
  3) Observe first disconnect.
  4) Immediately reconnect using same token, note 401 and new session creation in billing.

maya: I'll run the internal repro and attach tcpdump from the pod and the ALB flow logs. If we can capture the SYN/FIN sequence we can prove who closed first.

devon: Also check Cloudflare "origin keepalive" settings and any load balancer buffering. If CF buffers responses and ALB times out the origin, CF might keep client connection open and emit partial frames. That can leave app thinking it's still connected when ALB is closed.

allen: Customer is asking for a short-term config they can apply without code changes. Recommend: increase ALB idle timeout to 120s and set Cloudflare origin keepalive to 120s, enable server heartbeat every 20–25s. I asked them to try that and report back.

maya: Assigning follow-ups: maya - run repro + tcpdump, devon - audit auth refresh for reuse of tokens and short expiry, leo - reconcile billing and pause charges, allen - coordinate with customer and confirm mitigation.

oncall-bot: Reminder: paging window ends in 6h for INC-2026-874.

allen: For traceability: customer asked for root cause timeline and refund. I'll compile RCA after we have repro artifacts. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
